title: Rheumatoid factor and anti-CCP
what: This is a blood test from a vein. It looks for antibodies that can show up with joint inflammation.
why: For pain, swelling, and morning stiffness in the joints, especially in the hands and feet.
duration: the blood draw takes a few minutes; results usually come in 1 to 5 days
tell_doctor: Which joints hurt and for how long
If your hands feel stiff for more than half an hour in the morning
What medicines you take, especially steroids and painkillers

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Best in the morning, fasting for 8 to 12 hours. Water is fine. Check with the lab.

prepare.title: The day before
prepare.text: For 24 hours, no alcohol and no hard workouts. Best not to smoke in the morning.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own. Tell your doctor what you take. They will decide if anything should change.

bring: Past tests and joint X-rays, if you have them
steps: You sit down and rest your arm on the armrest
A band is tightened above your elbow
The skin is wiped with antiseptic
A quick prick, and blood fills a tube
The needle comes out, and a cotton pad is pressed on the spot
feel: A quick prick, like a pinch
Sometimes slight dizziness. Tell the nurse
after: Press the cotton pad for 3 to 5 minutes and keep your arm straight
You can eat right away and go back to your usual day
Results usually come in 1 to 5 days. The lab will tell you when
A rheumatologist will look at the result together with an exam

faq.q: Does a positive rheumatoid factor mean rheumatoid arthritis?
faq.a: Not always. It can show up in healthy people and in other illnesses. Your doctor makes the diagnosis.

faq.q: Why test anti-CCP together with rheumatoid factor?
faq.a: Together they are more accurate. Anti-CCP can turn positive earlier.

reminders.text: Rheumatoid factor and anti-CCP test tomorrow. Do not eat after dinner. Plain water is fine.
